sections.html: Marbled lungfishes (Protopterus aethiopicus) rank among the genuine survival artists. For respiration they are dependent on atmospheric air; if they are refused access to the surface, they can drown in the water (aquarium). Air breathing allows them a nearly amphibious way of life. They are able to withstand desiccation on floodplains by aestivating in cocoons. Contrary to some other lungfish species, the marbled lungfish is quite remarkably coloured and, at least as young individuals, well suited to keeping in aquaria.
